output.thesis: A tiny tube behind your eardrum lets air out easily and in reluctantly, so landing hurts more and a swallow fixes it.

beats.learns: She sits by the window as the plane climbs; her hand goes to her ear.
Behind the eardrum sits a pocket of air.
A thin tube runs from that pocket to the throat.
On the ground both sides are balanced.
The climb thins the cabin air.
The tube pops open and the air escapes: pop.
Landing is the opposite, and the tube stays shut.
Swallow, yawn or chew: the tube opens and her ears match the sky.

book.grammar: A friendly diagram: one idea per frame, a push on each realisation, a pull for the relief at the end.
book.palette: Sky blues and cream; a warm accent only on the ear and the pop.
book.performance: Small: a hand to the ear, a wince on the landing, relief at the swallow.
book.rhythm: A new card every 3-4 s; the landing beat holds longer for the reversal.
book.sound: A soft pop at 22 s, a cabin hum under everything.
